We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse: It's a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to another phenyl ring bearing an α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (anilide). So overall: p-tolyl-sulfonyl attached to phenyl which has a trans-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2? Actually the amide is C(=O)N attached to phenyl (c3ccccc3N) meaning an anilide with an aniline substituent (para? not specified). So the target has three key disconnections: 1) sulfonamide formation (sulfonyl chloride + amine). 2) amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine). 3) Doebner modification to form the α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde and malonic acid.

Thus retrosynthetic steps: Step 1: disconnect sulfonamide: break S-N bond, giving sulfonyl chloride (p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride) and aniline (the phenyl bearing the unsaturated amide). Actually the sulfonamide attaches to the p-tolyl sulfonyl group and the other phenyl (c2ccc...). So we get sulfonyl chloride: p-tolyl-SO2Cl (or p-tolylsulfonyl chloride) and the other phenyl sulfonamide precursor: the phenyl ring with the unsaturated amide attached (c2ccc(... )cc2) bearing an NH2? Wait the sulfonamide is NS(=O)(=O) attached to p-tolyl ring. The N is attached to the phenyl ring (c2...). So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the phenyl ring (c2...). So the disconnection yields: p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-Ph-CH3) and the aniline (the phenyl with the unsaturated amide and an NH2? Actually the N of sulfonamide is attached to the phenyl ring, not an NH2. So the phenyl part is a nucleophile (aniline) that attacks sulfonyl chloride to give sulfonamide. So the phenyl precursor is the same phenyl ring bearing the unsaturated amide and an NH (the N is the same as the sulfonamide N). So after disconnection, we have the phenyl ring with a free amine (aniline) attached to the unsaturated amide side chain. So precursor: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 (an aniline). That's the second step.

Step 2: disconnect amide: break C-N bond between carbonyl carbon and the aniline (c3ccccc3N). So we get carboxylic acid (the α,β-unsaturated acid) attached to phenyl (c2...), and aniline (c3ccccc3N). The α,β-unsaturated acid is formed via Doebner modification from aromatic aldehyde (the phenyl ring with aldehyde) and malonic acid. So precursor: aromatic aldehyde: c2ccc(/C= C/ C(=O)?) Wait the product after Doebner is α,β-unsaturated acid attached to phenyl. The aldehyde precursor is the same phenyl ring with an aldehyde at the position where the double bond will be. So the aldehyde is c2ccc(C=O)cc2? Actually the double bond is conjugated to the phenyl: /C=C/C(=O)N... So the aldehyde would be c2ccc(C=O)cc2 (para? not important). So we need to generate the α,β-unsaturated acid via Doebner from that aldehyde and malonic acid.

Thus step 3: Doebner modification: aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid (c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)...)cc2). So we need malonic acid as a reagent (commercial). The aldehyde is the phenyl aldehyde.

Thus we have three steps: (1) sulfonamide formation, (2) amide coupling, (3) Doebner modification.

Now we need to produce JSON route with type "mol" root target, children: reaction nodes with template IDs. We need to find appropriate template IDs for each reaction. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria with functional groups broken/formed.

We need templates for sulfonamide formation: functional_groups_broken: sulfonic? Actually sulfonyl chloride to sulfonamide: break S-Cl bond (maybe functional group "sulfonic" broken) and form sulfonamides. In functional groups list we have "sulfonic" and "sulfonamides". So we can search.
